name: Hullbreak CORROSION Tour Tee
description:
Black heavyweight cotton-poly with a bleach-damaged front print — the band name HULLBREAK in corroded industrial lettering above a cracked turbine graphic, the word CORROSION in smaller type below, and the tour dates printed down the left sleeve: seventeen the Gray Zone-level venues across the Great Lakes corridor, year 2198. The back has a full cityscape of the lower GLMZ waterfront rendered in a single-color white screenprint, partially cracked from washing.

Hullbreak is a post-industrial noise band that has never played above Tier 2. Their shows are loud, dangerous, and technically unpermitted in most of the venues they play anyway. This shirt is a badge of having been there — in the pit, in the dark, in the noise. Counterfeits exist but the real ones have a small stamped number on the interior tag (1 through 500, the original run).
what_it_says: I was there. I survived it. I liked it.
worn_by: the Gray Zone music scene regulars
story_hooks: The shirt's tour dates include a venue that burned down the night of the show — anyone wearing one of the originals was in that building.
A Spire music collector is quietly paying premium prices for authenticated originals; someone in the Gray Zone has six of them and doesn't know what they're worth.
One of the numbered shirts (No. 7) was worn by someone who disappeared after the final tour date — the shirt has become an urban legend in certain the Gray Zone circles.

physical_description.visual_profile: A worn, intentionally damaged band tee that reads as authentically weathered rather than artificially distressed. The front features aggressive industrial lettering with a deliberate bleach-corroded aesthetic, creating an impression of chemical degradation. The silhouette is relaxed and slightly oversized, typical of underground music merchandise. The back cityscape print dominates visually, giving the wearer a distinctly subversive, anti-corporate presence.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed, slightly oversized through the chest and shoulders. Straight cut through the torso with a natural drape. Hem sits at mid-hip. Sleeve length reaches mid-bicep with a comfortable, unstretched opening.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight cotton-poly blend (60/40), durable enough to withstand multiple pit encounters and harsh washing cycles without immediate degradation.
physical_description.texture: Crisp and dense when new, breaking in to a soft, worn-in feel after use. The screenprint has a slightly raised, tactile quality; the bleach damage creates subtle puckering and thinned patches in the cotton weave. Back print shows intentional cracking from legitimate wear, not artificial aging.
physical_description.color_scheme: Solid black base with white screenprinted graphics front and back. The bleach damage on the front creates irregular pale gray and cream zones, giving organic variation. No additional accent colors.
physical_description.closures: None — crew neck pullover with raw-edge construction typical of budget band merch.
distinctive_features: Front bleach-corroded HULLBREAK lettering in jagged industrial font
Cracked turbine graphic beneath band name
Left sleeve tour dates: seventeen Shelf-level venue names and dates (2198)
Full white cityscape screenprint on back (lower GLMZ waterfront motif)
Deliberately cracked back print from authentic wear
Interior tag stamped with serial number (1–500 original run)
Faded, slightly yellowed areas from sweat and UV exposure
Minor pilling on chest from friction in the pit
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4–5 street/sub-grade. The handmade merch table origin, raw construction, and deliberate damage signal working-class underground culture, not aspirational corporate branding.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this shirt announces attendance at an illegal or semi-legal noise show, alignment with post-industrial counter-culture, and rejection of mainstream music venues. It's a membership badge in a specific GLMZ subcommunity. Counterfeits are known to exist, making the stamped serial number a subtle flex among collectors.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and authentically weathered. Fading concentrated on shoulders and chest from repeated wear. Back print genuinely cracked from legitimate washing. Front bleach damage remains crisp but shows light fading. Edges slightly curled from aging.
